claims.text: Conventional additive-free ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has notable porosity.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 is susceptible to failure during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Adding a trace amount of silicon to ZrB2 induces a transient liquid phase during sintering.
Silicon addition lowers the effective ZrB2 sintering temperature to approximately 2000 °C.
The proposed transient liquid phase improves grain-boundary wetting.
The proposed transient liquid phase enhances mass transport and particle rearrangement.
Enhanced mass transport, wetting, and particle rearrangement accelerate densification of silicon-doped ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 sintered at approximately 2000 °C will have less residual porosity than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Residual pores provide infiltration paths for a liquid plating bath.
Infiltration of the plating bath through residual pores causes hole formation and degradation.
Reducing residual porosity will reduce hole formation during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 sintered at approximately 2000 °C will achieve densification comparable to or better than additive-free ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will retain better structural integrity after long-term plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
